race_name: Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds

top_categories.workout_context: 11,239ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
At Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
172ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.

Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds' paved mountain road — sea level to 3,275m through forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 65 miles.
11,239ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds. Train it until it feels boring.
65 miles on paved mountain road — sea level to 3,275m through burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Base fitness for Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Low-cadence force work for 11,239ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on paved mountain road — sea level to 3,275m through. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds’s 65 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds with 11,239ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%. Temperature drop of 20-25C from coastal start to alpine summit — you start in summer and finish in winter; High-altitude cold at 3,275m — wind chill can drive effective temperatures well below freezing.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Taiwan KOM Challenge — The Ascent to the Clouds requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on paved mountain road — sea level to 3,275m through taroko gorge to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 65 miles of paved mountain road — sea level to 3,275m through taroko gorge in Hualien (Qixingtan Beach) to Wuling Pass, Taiwan.
